body: Aha, yep, that works :) Changes merged in.
@dsnopek @Repiteo It would be great to get this one merged for dev2.

So the basic answer, as I see it, is:

* Object IDs are safer, in the sense that there's no such thing as an unknowably invalid object ID. You can always check to see if it's a valid ID; there's no way to check if it's a valid pointer. This makes it a safer interface for the system in general.
* With the C++ GDExtension layer, converting a pointer to an active instance type requires an internal-only API, though nothing *currently* prevents you from calling it. (But also, nothing prevents the C++ GDExtension devs from changing it to be `private` and allowing internal access only via `friend`.)
* With the C# GodotSharp layer, converting a pointer to an active instance type requires an internal-only API, but in this case the language enforces "internal", so you either need to change GodotSharp itself to allow this or use reflection to punch through C#'s permission system.
* In both cases, you can just call the appropriate GDExtension function to get an active instance from the instance ID; this is already supported and exposed.

The problem is that external languages *can't use pointers directly*, they have to wrap it in whatever their GDExtension layer expects, and that's not a thing that GDExtension implementations are usually built for. `godot::ObjectDB::get_instance()` and `GodotObject.InstanceFromId()` both exist, but there isn't an exposed equivalent that takes a pointer (and arguably there shouldn't be).

In a theoretically ideal world, the DLL binding would just provide a GodotInstance . . . but this is an impossible chicken-and-egg problem, because calling a function that provides a GodotInstance requires a working GDExtension/GodotSharp layer, which can't exist until we call the function. Which is also why the LibGodot start function has to be a raw exposed dynamic-library function and can't just be part of GDExtension in the first place.

> * With the C++ GDExtension layer, converting a pointer to an active instance type requires an internal-only API, though nothing _currently_ prevents you from calling it. (But also, nothing prevents the C++ GDExtension devs from changing it to be `private` and allowing internal access only via `friend`.)

I don't think we should be deciding how this API works based on what godot-cpp (or any GDExtension binding) is currently doing. I would expect that godot-cpp will require some (small) changes in order to properly support LibGodot. I'm less familiar with the C# side, but I would expect that to be true there as well.

I think we should only be looking at this in the context of the GDExtension interface, and it provides us with both `object_get_instance_from_id()` and `object_get_instance_id()` which allow freely converting between object pointers and IDs.

> * Object IDs are safer, in the sense that there's no such thing as an unknowably invalid object ID. You can always check to see if it's a valid ID; there's no way to check if it's a valid pointer. This makes it a safer interface for the system in general.

This isn't a very compelling argument to me. For LibGodot to work, the `GodotInstance` object needs to remain valid from when it's created until it's explicitly destroyed. The idea that you could call `libgodot_create_godot_instance()`, and it might not be valid by the time you call `libgodot_destroy_godot_instance()` is silly.

We can document that the instance will remain valid until explicitly destroyed, and then make sure to keep that promise. Then it's only the caller of this API that can make the pointer invalid, and so it's on them to make sure not to use it after they've called `libgodot_destroy_godot_instance()`.

> I would expect that godot-cpp will require some (small) changes in order to properly support LibGodot. I'm less familiar with the C# side, but I would expect that to be true there as well.

For what it's worth, with this API change, godot-cpp works seamlessly in its current state. I would expect this to be true of most GDExtension layers.

GodotSharp does require a few changes so it can accept starting on top of an already-existing .NET environment.

> I think we should only be looking at this in the context of the GDExtension interface, and it provides us with both object_get_instance_from_id() and object_get_instance_id() which allow freely converting between object pointers and IDs.

I agree, but the problem is that there's no agreed-upon way to pass in an opaque direct pointer and get either a working GDExtension interface or an ID. The GDExtension system is built around two concepts of object references, "the GDExtension-wrapped version" and "IDs". That's why I'm trying to change this to "just rely on the ID". And as far as I know, the existing GDExtension stuff doesn't currently provide a solution for "given a pointer, no, really, actually the pointer, not the thing your GDExtension has wrapped, please give me the ID/wrapped version".

I guess I'm not sure what the downside of this approach is; it slots more easily into the existing system and removes the need for changes to existing libraries.

> I guess I'm not sure what the downside of this approach is; it slots more easily into the existing system and removes the need for changes to existing libraries.

There isn't really a downside, other than I think most folks who call `libgodot_create_godot_instance()` (and get an object ID) will probably immediately call `object_get_instance_from_id()`, because I suspect most GDExtensions bindings (after being modified to accommodate LibGodot) will want the object pointer.

So, I'm pretty much fine with the change itself, I just don't agree with the reasons that have been given for it. If the caller wants the object ID, we don't need this PR - they can just call `object_get_instance_id()` on the returned object pointer.

Whether we use object IDs vs object pointers isn't a material difference, because regardless of what `libgodot_create_godot_instance()` returns, you can convert to the other thing via `object_get_instance_from_id()` or `object_get_instance_id()`.

So I do still think the ID thing is safer, but I mostly pulled that from Raul's commentary, and the part I care about the most is the whole "doesn't require custom changes to every GDExtension layer" thing. Willing to accept that as the primary reason instead? :V

I'll defer to @dsnopek to decide whether it makes sense to use a pointer or ObjectID in the exposed API. I only mentioned using ObjectID because I slightly remember it should be preferred so we can validate the Object instead of crashing, but that was in a different context so it may not be relevant.

From C#, you could try `object_get_instance_id` as @dsnopek suggested, and then use that ID with `GodotObject.InstanceFromId`.

Alternatively, as you mentioned, you can use reflection if you really need to use `InteropUtils.UnmanagedGetManaged`. I don't see us changing this API in GodotSharp, so we shouldn't break you.

> the part I care about the most is the whole "doesn't require custom changes to every GDExtension layer" thing

I don't think these are "custom changes" - this is GDExtension bindings updating to support LibGodot, same as they update for any new features that are added to `gdextension_interface.h`.

We can chat about this more at the GDExtension team meeting later, but perhaps it would be good to go back up to a high level:

1. Who are the APIs added in `libgodot.h` intended to be used by?
2. How will LibGodot be distributed to and used by developers?

My answers would be (1) the functions in `libgodot.h` are intended to be called by GDExtension bindings, and (2) in 99% of cases, I imagine that LibGodot will be distributed as part of GDExtension bindings which provide their own APIs for starting LibGodot (ie. the developers aren't going to be directly calling `libgodot_create_godot_instance()`, they'll use an API provided by the bindings).

Let's imagine a theoretical Python binding for GDExtension (there are a couple, I'm not thinking of a specific real one).

If a developer wants to use LibGodot with this Python binding: they should NOT be building their own LibGodot from source, writing some C glue code to call `libgodot_create_godot_instance()`, and then passing the result to some function in the Python binding to make a wrapper object.

Instead, I think the ideal workflow would be that the Python bindings project makes a build which includes LibGodot and provides a friendly Pythonic API for creating the `GodotInstance`. And the developer simply has to run `pip install python-libgodot==4.6.1` to install this package and start using it.

And, so, if we're imagining that GDExtension bindings will be adopting LibGodot in this way (which is what I've personally been imagining) then the bindings will be updated to support LibGodot. And since they will be modified anyway, there's no reason to worry about what public APIs they have presently for converting from an object pointer or ID to the wrapper object.

Based on our discussion yesterday in the meeting, I am leaning towards the following:

- Keep the interface as it is now with GDExtensionObjectPtr as the return value. The contract is that libgodot_create_godot_instance() will return a valid object or NULL, so there is no risk of receiving an invalid pointer. In most cases the host process will want to call methods on the returned object immediately, so returning an object reference is probably more appropriate than returning an object id.

- Encourage GDExtension binding developers to expose a function that can convert raw GDExtensionObjectPtr pointers to wrapped objects. A corresponding PR should be created for godot-cpp. (We can talk about the logistics of this separately.)

- In the specific case of using the legacy (frozen?) C# binding, the following workaround should work:

  - In the LibGodot init function, the host process resolves and stores the object_get_instance_id function using the GDExtensionInterfaceGetProcAddress function received as a parameter.
  - After libgodot_create_godot_instance() returns, the host process calls the stored object_get_instance_id function to get the GDObjectInstanceID of the GDExtensionObjectPtr pointer.
  - Use the received object id to initialize the GodotSharp binding.
  
 This method should work for any LibGodot user in any language, without the need to change the LibGodot / GDExtension interface already provided by Godot.
 
 @zorbathut @dsnopek What do you think about this solution?
I admit I'm still skeptical about this because I think it's going to be a pain for endusers for quite a while, but it's fine for me, so, sure.
